title: Hungarian raids in the West
fact_summary: From the 860s to the 950s, Latin writers record Hungarian armies raiding Frankish lands, Italy and beyond, sometimes as allies or paid to leave. The written sources on this map follow them from first appearance to defeat.

claims.text: The Annals of St-Bertin, under 862, record enemies “previously unknown”, called Ungri, ravaging the kingdom of Louis.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Liudprand of Cremona, writing around 960, says that almost all nations had experienced the Hungarians' savagery.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: He reports that in 943 King Hugh of Italy paid them to make peace and sent them on towards Spain.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A Metz annal says that by 955 they had entered Lothar's kingdom for the fourth time, and that Otto defeated them that year.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: In 892 the Hungarians came with an army to join King Arnulf's campaign against the Moravians.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: In 899–900 they beat an Italian army on the Brenta and then crossed the Enns into Bavaria, laying waste fifty miles in a day.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: From 907 to 910 Regino's continuator lists a defeat every year or two: the Bavarians and their duke in 907, Saxony and Thuringia in 908, Alamannia in 909, the Franks in 910.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: Widukind says King Henry bought nine years of peace by giving back a captured Hungarian leader “with other gifts”, and later speaks of “the usual gifts” that Hungarian envoys came to collect.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: He says that in 955 the Hungarian army was destroyed over three days, and three of its leaders hanged.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

open_questions.text: Why did the raids happen: for plunder, for payment, or as hired troops in other rulers' wars?
Did the raids end because of one defeat in 955, or for wider reasons?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
